articles.title: Wall Street slips ahead of inflation data, crude oil surges
articles.excerpt:
Wall Street stocks edged lower on Monday as investors weighed higher oil prices and looked ahead to a busy week of economic data, including fresh readings on inflation.

In early trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.2 percent at 53,937.14. The broad-based S&P 500 dipped 0.1 percent to 7,753.90, while the tech-rich Nasdaq Composite Index shed 0.2 percent to 26,638.35.

Oil prices climbed around 1.5% after Iran said it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the United States met a series of demands, including compensation for war-related damage. The development added to concerns about potential disruptions to global energy supplies.

Brent crude futures rallied 3.06% to $8

articles.title: Tata Technologies among 5 stocks flashing bullish signals. Upside on cards?
articles.excerpt:
On August 7, five Nifty500 stocks that gained more than 4% featured on StockEdge’s ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to its technical scan data.

A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis, formed when a stock opens at or near its low and closes at or near its high. The pattern appears as a long white or green candle with little to no upper or lower shadow, signalling strong buying pressure throughout the session.

Traders often view the pattern as an indication that buyers remained firmly in control from the opening to the close, potentially signalling further strength.
